articles.title: Atari Is Re-Releasing 39 Atari 2600 Games on Working, Physical Cartridges
articles.summary: Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection. The unexpected project reunites Activision with Atari after almost 50 years.
body: The full set of working, physical game cartridges includes 39 classic Activision games, like Pitfall!, River Raid, and Kaboom!, and there will be three ways to purchase them.

Individual, “Standard Edition” versions of 12 of the games will be available from November for USD$35 each. The 12 games include Pitfall!, River Raid, Megamania, Enduro, Kaboom!, H.E.R.O., Pressure Cooker, Private Eye, River Raid II, Keystone Kapers, The Activision Decathlon, and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns (although Atari notes The Activision Decathlon and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns will actually ship at a later date than the other titles). The Standard Edition games feature full packaging and a printed, colour manual inspired by the original releases. They’ll be compatible with Atari 2600+ and Atari 7800+ consoles, as well as original Atari 2600 and 7800 hardware.

articles.title: Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Remake Preview: Hands-On with Ubisoft’s Reborn Strategy Classic - Gamescom 2026
articles.summary: In a year where Ubisoft announced and shipped the Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag remake, a revival of Heroes of Might and Magic 3 might not be the highest-profile remake project, but it’s an appreciated one nevertheless.
body: For the uninitiated, Heroes of Might and Magic is a strategy game series where players take on the roles of factions that guide armies into battles on an overworld map. Each faction, led by a Hero, explores a map with multiple points of interest, recruiting new soldiers, gaining resources, and eventually clashing with enemy troops. In those clashes, players move their units around a side-view battlefield broken into hexagonal panels and fight to be the last group standing for their hero.

All this gameplay is intact in the remake, making Heroes of Might and Magic III feel like the classic that fans have known and loved over the last few decades with a new coat of paint. Though Heroes of Might and Magic III was remastered by Ubisoft a decade ago, the 2026 title is a true top-to-bottom remake of the game in terms of visuals, while leaving the gameplay relatively untouched.

articles.title: The Biggest Gaming Stories That Happened Since GTA 5 Came Out 13 Years Ago
articles.summary: The long, long wait for GTA 6 is coming to an end, as the game's November 19 release date approaches. Yes, there have been many leaks, but the genuine article arrives soon. It's been 13 years since GTA 5 launched in September 2013, and a lot has happened in the world of video games since then.
body: In this post, we're running through some of the most notable gaming events and stories since GTA 5 launched more than a decade ago. To be sure, this is not an exhaustive list, and it does not touch on the many real-world, non-gaming high-profile events that have transpired. This list is all about big gaming stories, of which there have been many.

The COVID-19 pandemic, which took hold in early 2020, had a massive impact on the world, of course, including the video game industry. Due to stay-at-home orders and general social distancing policies, people spent more time--and money--on things they could do at home. Naturally, home gym and fitness equipment sales soared, but so did spending on entertainment like video games.

To help in her journey, she will discover and adopt mysterious creatures known as Hântu, which she can use to help her fight, get through tough spots with their abilities, and to move about the world. In this new Volcanic biome, Abi will run into at least three Hântu, Razzle (explosive projectiles that burn and multiply), Mokul (summons pyroclastic rain that scorches an area), and Furioso (throws magma that spreads between enemies).

As for Röhe, this Moth Boss is actually a young hunter from the Frostlands who will challenge Abi in this new region. To make it through the test set in a "magma-lit arena," Abi will have to perfet her movement, combat skills, and Hântu abilities.

articles.title: Metro 2039 Developers on How Russia's Invasion of Ukraine Changed Their Plans
articles.summary: After finishing the four-or-so-hour preview build of Metro 2039, the upcoming first-person shooter sequel from Ukrainian developer 4A Games and falling completely in love with it, I reached out to the team to ask some questions about how they've approached the latest entry in their post-apocalyptic…
body: "First of all, it's impacted the team," said creative director Andriy "MLS" Shevchenko. "The world changes the team completely, their way of being, their way of thinking, and their way of understanding what's going on in general. So automatically it brings new visions and new philosophy into the game through the team. And everything else is just details. Story changed? Yes. Some gameplay elements changed? Yes. But first of all, it's the team."

"And I would say that effect on the team did actually directly affect the story in the way that previous Metro games were about the prevention of war," said executive producer Jon Bloch. "And when Russia started its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, it brought war to our doorsteps and we had to change our approach about what kind of story we wanted to tell. We wanted to tell now the consequences of war, what happens when war comes to you. And so it was a pretty major change to what we were doing. We had to try to see from a production standpoint what we could save and what needed to change. We tried to save as much as we could, but quite a lot of our plans changed overnight."

articles.title: 10 Years Ago, Anime’s Most Powerful Quote Is Still an All Time Classic
articles.summary: The "chosen one" is one of the oldest tricks in the storytelling playbook, and for good reason. There is something inherently compelling about watching an ordinary person discover they are extraordinary. It’s foretold that Anakin Skywalker is destined to bring balance to the Force in Star Wars.
body: But what happens when being the "chosen one" is just plain exhausting? That’s the exact question Mob Psycho 100 weaponizes. On paper, Shigeo “Mob” Kageyama looks like the undisputed poster boy for power fantasy. He’s an absurdly gifted psychic capable of flattening entire city blocks or rewriting reality the second his emotions spike. He possesses almost every classic shonen hallmark: frightening talent, overwhelming power, and the latent capability to reshape the world.

It’s a quintessentially Reigen line. Here’s a charming fraud with zero psychic talent standing next to a living, breathing natural disaster, reassuring him that his identity isn't tied to his output. Mob’s life shouldn’t be shackled by his absurd abilities, the people who fear him, or some cosmic mandate. His life belongs solely to him.

Framing his identity this way completely flips the genre on its head. Mob is undeniably gifted, but the series refuses to let that gift define his human value. His psychic abilities are spectacular and occasionally terrifying, but they aren't what make him worthy of empathy or connection.
points: The "chosen one" is one of the oldest tricks in the storytelling playbook, and for good reason.
There is something inherently compelling about watching an ordinary person discover they are extraordinary.
It’s foretold that Anakin Skywalker is destined to bring balance to the Force in Star Wars.
That’s the exact question Mob Psycho 100 weaponizes.

I played the game's demo build for Gamescom remotely before heading out to the event, and it was the perfect way to spend a Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Metro 2039 is a game about war that actually has something to say
articles.summary: Earlier this year, publisher Deep Silver and developer 4A Studios published a blog post outlining its vision for Metro 2039. The studio revealed the game - being developed primarily in Ukraine amid the continued Russian invasion - is darker and focuses on the "cost of silence, the horrors of…
body: "I think the landscape has changed significantly [since we developed the previous games in the series]," says Jon Bloch, executive producer at 4A Games, when I ask him if the context of Metro 2039's production has altered the vision for the sequel. "The previous games were about preventing war; the themes and the morals and all that supported this idea that revolved around 'how do we as humans stop the cycle that we keep finding ourselves in'. And when Russia started its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, that brought war to our doorstep. Now, our team has been living in a state of war for the last four and a half years. And that changes things. Significantly."

As 4A navigates the reality of making a video game during war time, Bloch says the studio needs to reflect on "the consequences of war", and - essentially - write what it knows. Metro 2039 was never an apolitical series, not by any means, but its assessment and commentary on the politics of war was more detached. More 'what if'.

articles.title: Metro 2039 Dev Reveals How the Ukraine War Led to the Series’ Darkest Game Yet
articles.summary: Due to launch in February 2027, Metro 2039 is the next chapter in the story that began in 2010 with Metro 2033. The grim first-person shooters are based on the works of novelist Dmitry Glukhovsky, who first partnered with 4A Games to bring his dark vision to life.
body: Life feels much different today than it did in 2019, when Deep Silver published Metro Exodus on PC and consoles. The people of Ukraine have endured more impactful changes than most. On February 24, 2022, Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The two nations have remained locked in conflict ever since, at great cost to the many innocent citizens caught in a power struggle they never wanted. For the developers at 4A Games, who have been working on the very dark Metro 2039, that event was impossible to ignore.
In a video interview with Polygon, Metro 2039’s executive producer, Jon Bloch, discussed the shift that occurred in the game’s development, following Russia’s invasion.

“We had to rethink our story,” Bloch told Polygon. “Ideas we had of things that we had to get right with the first iteration of the game completely changed, so now the story was going to be the most important thing… We needed to basically take all the emotions of the team and everything that the team and everyone in Ukraine is going through and find a way to tell the right story.”

articles.title: Activision Embraces Physical Games With 39 Classic Rereleases
articles.summary: Amid a dour outlook for physical games, two publishers are teaming up to buck that trend: Atari is teaming up with Activision to rerelease some of the Atari 2600's most iconic games.
body: If you're looking to collect them all, though, be prepared to spend up to $1,000.

Long before Activision was known for making Call of Duty, the studio got its start developing games for the Atari 2600. Activision, which was founded by former Atari employees, was responsible for some of the console's best games, including Pitfall! and River Raid. Despite that history, Activision distanced itself from its roots as time went on, especially after getting acquired by Microsoft in 2023. The newfound collaboration will unlock a treasure trove of buried history for the first time in decades.

The Atari x Activision Collection's period-accurate cartridges will be functional on classic consoles, as well as the modern Atari 2600+ and Atari 7800+ systems. A dozen of the 39 games will launch as Standard Edition cartridges that will be available to purchase for $34.99 each. Pitfall!, River Raid, Megamania, Enduro, and more will be available to purchase individually in November, while The Activision Decathlon and Pitfall 2: Lost Caverns will ship at a later date.

articles.title: I'm not a fan of Heroes of Might & Magic 3, but I can recognise that Ubisoft have done a faithful job of recreating the much-loved turn-based strategy RPG
articles.summary: Heroes of Might & Magic is having a moment. Not only are publishers Hooded Horse and Ubisoft backing the development of Unfrozen's Heroes of Might & Magic: Olden Era, the first new game in the series in more than a decade, but Ubisoft have revealed they're completely remaking the series'…
body: While there are many quality of life improvements in the remake, Ubisoft aims to keep its spirit as close to the original as possible. There is a new three-mission prelude to get you into the story and teach you the game's systems but, after that, you're into the thick of the original campaign and its two expansions – Armageddon's Blade and The Shadow of Death. This also means you'll have all nine factions to play with.

I've played the remake for a few hours already and I'll get into my thoughts on that in a moment. But, the most telling thing about the remake is that it supports all the custom maps and campaigns players have made for the past 25 years. Ubisoft showed how you can import any original map file into Might & Magic 3 Remake's map creator and it will build a modern-looking level from the old data. It's a wonderful way to support the Heroes of Might & Magic 3 players who are still playing decades on from its release.

articles.title: Gravhounds Reveal Trailer Sends Good Boys Into A Sci-Fi Battle
articles.summary: Gamescom Opening Night Live is always full of surprises, and this year, indie developer Octopus Panic made a splash with a first look at its new action-builder game Gravhounds.
body: Although the trailer states that the titular Gravhounds have been "bred" for this life, their humanoid appearance suggests more than a little genetic engineering was responsible for this turn of events. In fact, there's no sign of human life at all on this hostile alien world, but the Gravhounds themselves seem human enough.

The gameplay supports 1-4 players as they attempt to build up resources for a new colony while holding on to the potential promise of coming home. Upgrades appear to play a major role in the main characters' survival, especially when they get overwhelmed by alien forces that really don't want them around at all.

According to Gravhounds' Steam page, the game's early-access period will last at least six months. It will "include the core Gravhound experience," but we plan to expand its breadth, depth, and replayability on the road to 1.0," reads the statement. Both solo and co-op campaigns will be playable during this initial release.
Gravhounds' early-access release will hit Xbox Series X|S and PC on November 2. It will also be available on day one with Xbox Game Pass.

articles.title: Ubisoft forgot to make sure the Steam release of Heroes of Might & Magic 3 included the actual game
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: The HD rerelease of Heroes of Might & Magic 3 from 2015 used to be the only way to get the strategy classic on Steam, leaving many players frustrated since it lacked the expansions and the random map generator. Ask fans of the series, and they'd tell you to get the original version from GOG instead.

So it should be an easy win for Ubisoft that the series' current owner finally decided to put the original version, complete with its expansions Armageddon's Blade and The Shadow of Death, on Steam at last. Its current user review rating of 80% negative suggests otherwise.

Fork out $10 for it and you'll find an install that's only 23.49 KB big, which gives a "dummy executable" error message when you try to launch it. Because Heroes of Might & Magic 3 on Steam does not come with Heroes of Might & Magic 3. Somebody forgot to include the actual game files with the game.

I'm sure this will be fixed soon, perhaps when France wakes up, but in the meantime the complete edition on GOG is still the best version and it's currently on sale for half-price. Here's hoping the upcoming remake has a smoother launch, you know, like one where they actually remember to include the game.

videos.title: Everything Announced at Opening Night Live 2026
videos.summary: Tons of games were shown off this year at the gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 showcase. Among the many was the highly anticipated reveal of the Witcher 3's expansion and remaster, Songs of the Past.
points: Tons of games were shown off this year at the gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 showcase.
Among the many was the highly anticipated reveal of the Witcher 3's expansion and remaster, Songs of the Past.
We got an in-depth look at all the quality of life changes coming with the Witcher 3 Remastered and some story beats of where Songs of the Past will lead.
Here's everything that was announced at ONL 2026.
